label: LLM
description: AI language model completion. Which service serves it comes from a wired provider node (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, or a custom endpoint); sampling parameters come from a wired LlmParams node, and without one the defaults apply. A conversation is kept in a file that each call adds its turn to (`historyFile`); wired LLM Tool declarations turn on tool calling. For an agent that calls tools until it is done: run turns in a sequential Loop carrying the conversation file. Each turn takes the file on `historyFile` and the LLM Tools on `tools` (several through a List). When the model asks for tools, `toolCalls` pulses a List[ToolCall], each `{ id, name, arguments }` with `arguments` as raw JSON text; run them in a sequential Loop over `toolCalls` that carries the file, a Switch on the call's `name` (one `equals` case per tool) gating each tool's node, and add each result to the file with a Chat Message node (see its description). The file that loop hands back feeds the next turn, and the turns stop when one answers with no `toolCalls` pulse.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.description: The prompt to send, appended as the newest user message. Optional when a `historyFile` is wired (a tool-result round re-enters with the conversation alone).

inputs.name: historyFile
inputs.description: The conversation so far, kept in a stored file (a previous call's or a Chat Message node's `historyFile` output, or a file holding `[]` to start one that later runs will continue: store it in the project scope). This call's turn is added to this same file, in place, and the file comes out on `historyFile`. Unwired, the call starts from no conversation.

inputs.name: media
inputs.description: Media attached to this prompt: one stored image, audio clip, or video, or a list of them.

inputs.name: provider
inputs.description: The provider (wire an OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, or Custom Provider node's output): which service, which model, whose credential the call spends. Always wire one of those nodes; never build this value by hand or pass it through a port typed JsonDict (a group that carries it declares the port as LlmProvider). The provider node holds the connection, so the credential never appears in the program.

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: Optional LlmParams node carrying the sampling settings (system prompt, temperature, ...). Unwired, the defaults apply.

inputs.name: tools
inputs.description: Tool declarations the model may call: one LLM Tool node's output, or a list of them.

inputs.name: toolChoice
inputs.label: Tool choice
inputs.description: Only used when tools are wired: auto lets the model decide, required forces a call, none forbids one.

inputs.name: parseJson
inputs.label: Parse JSON
inputs.description: Parse and repair JSON from the response (changes output to Dict). With it on, declare output ports named after the JSON's keys (`-> (verdict: String, score: Number)`) and each key comes out as its own port; `response` then only matters when something reads the whole object.

inputs.name: autoCache
inputs.label: Automatic prompt caching
inputs.description: On: when the conversation carries no cache mark, the request marks the system message and the last message before this call's new turn, so a chain of calls reuses its stable prefix. The marks live on the request alone: the `historyFile` keeps the conversation as written, so the next call in the chain places its own. A conversation that already carries marks (Chat Message's `cacheBreakpoint`) is sent as placed.

outputs.name: response
outputs.description: The reply. Declare its type in the source: `String` without parseJson; with parseJson, prefer one output port per JSON key (`-> (verdict: String)`) and read `response` only when something needs the whole object (then `JsonDict` or a record type).

outputs.name: historyFile
outputs.description: The conversation including this call, kept in a file: the `historyFile` that came in, with this call's user message and reply added to it in place (same file, next version), or, when none came in, a new file holding this turn, kept past the run. Wire it into the next call's or Chat Message node's `historyFile`. Left unwired with no file in, the call is a one-shot and keeps nothing.

outputs.name: toolCalls
outputs.description: The tool calls the model made, if any (each with the raw JSON text of its arguments). Pulses only when the model called tools; append each result with a Chat Message node (role: tool) and wire the `historyFile` back into the next LLM call. A call left without an answer (the run stopped before its result was appended) is answered `cancelled` by the next call on its own, so the conversation keeps working.

then.message: '{id}' declares output ports ({custom_outputs}) that only fire with parseJson: true; turn it on, or drop the ports and read `response`
